title: AI Industry Evidence Monitor
method: Deterministic, source-bound aggregation. No LLM-generated numeric assertions.

cards.label: EU enterprise AI use
cards.description: EU27, surveyed businesses with 10+ employed persons; official statistic.

cards.label: Surveyed organizations using AI
cards.description: McKinsey survey across geographies: any-function use, including pilots.

cards.label: Daily data source health
cards.description: Only registered automatic sources, not all AI research websites.

cards.label: Core publication coverage
cards.description: Article index records, not readership or importance.

findings.title: EU business AI-use share changed +6.47 pp versus 2024
findings.text: Eurostat reports 19.95% in 2025 versus 13.48% in 2024, an increase of 6.47 percentage points. This is adoption, not realized ROI.

findings.title: Surveyed organizations' reported AI use changed +10.00 pp versus 2024
findings.text: The OWID/McKinsey all-geographies survey reports 88.00% in 2025 versus 78.00% in 2024. It covers use in at least one function and is not directly comparable with Eurostat.

findings.title: Regional survey spread: 9.0 pp in 2025
findings.text: Within the same OWID/McKinsey organization-use survey, Europe records 91.0% and Asia-Pacific records 82.0%, a 9.0 percentage-point observed range. Regional definitions overlap and sampling/weighting differ; this does not establish causality or representative country-level demand.

findings.title: 317 indexed links; 207 from core publisher feeds
findings.text: Counts reflect the configured RSS/Atom feeds and article classifications, not global research investment or market demand. Source-mix changes can alter topic proportions.

findings.title: No defensible daily usage-growth trend yet
findings.text: Only 1 unique daily snapshot date(s) are stored. At least two comparable dates for the same entity and metric are required to compute changes. List prices and GitHub stars are proxies, not token volume or commercial revenue.

charts.title: EU27 business AI use · Eurostat
charts.caveat: Official ICT survey, enterprises with 10+ employed persons, percentage using at least one AI technology.

charts.title: AI use within surveyed organizations · OWID/McKinsey
charts.caveat: Self-reported AI use in any business function, across surveyed organizations; includes experimentation/pilots. Not the same population as Eurostat.

charts.title: Regional AI use · same organization survey
charts.caveat: Same survey and year; regions can overlap (Greater China is part of Asia-Pacific). Not a census, not production ROI; regional percentages are not additive.

charts.title: Input model list prices by provider
charts.caveat: Unweighted median of the most recently-created model entries sampled per provider (up to 12), excluding free prices. This is neither realized transaction pricing nor market share, and differs by model mix.

charts.title: Output model list prices by provider
charts.caveat: Unweighted median of the most recently-created model entries sampled per provider (up to 12), excluding free prices. This is neither realized transaction pricing nor market share, and differs by model mix.

charts.title: Model output/input list-price multiples
charts.caveat: Median of output price divided by input price for matched model IDs with positive prices. This is a posted tariff asymmetry, not inference cost, usage volume, or company margin.

charts.title: Research archive coverage by topic
charts.caveat: Core-feeds-only article counts are **coverage of configured feeds**. They are not an industry topic-share survey, and publisher publication volume varies.

charts.title: Tracked AI engineering repositories · GitHub stars
charts.caveat: Cumulative developer-interest signal in a selected set of repositories, not unique users, adoption, revenue, or an unbiased ecosystem ranking.

coverage_gaps.title: Verified AI-specific revenue
coverage_gaps.reason: No audited AI-only revenue series is connected. Cloud segment revenue is not equivalent to AI revenue.

coverage_gaps.title: Representative enterprise AI payments
coverage_gaps.reason: Ramp and private purchase/payment data remain licensed or sample-limited.

coverage_gaps.title: Completed agent actions and transactions
coverage_gaps.reason: No comparable transaction/fulfillment outcomes dataset is connected.

coverage_gaps.title: AI infrastructure return on invested capital
coverage_gaps.reason: Even with company-wide audited PPE cash spending, AI-specific expenditure, leasing, contribution profits and segment revenue are not isolated.

research_note: Adoption surveys, API model list prices, selected repository popularity, and publisher article counts measure different populations and outcomes. No causal claims or cross-dataset market shares can be made without compatible denominators.
